name: Duo
summary: Duo is Cisco's multi-factor authentication service, sold in four editions from a free tier for 10 users to $9 per user per month. Risk-based authentication sits in the $6 Advantage edition and above, so the $3 Essentials edition does not include it.

evidence.capability: second-factor methods such as app push or hardware keys

facts.text: Duo's authentication methods page describes approving a login with a tap in the Duo Mobile app and lists FIDO2 security keys.

Duo's documentation says Risk-Based Authentication is deployed through policies for Duo Advantage and Duo Premier customers and steps up to the most secure factors when it sees a known attack pattern or anomaly, such as unrealistic travel.
Administrators can add users manually, run bulk enrollment from a list of usernames and emails, send enrollment emails, and generate one-time enrollment codes that expire after 24 hours by default.
Admins can define separate enrollment and account management policies that control what users see during enrollment.
Paid editions are bought in increments of 10 licenses below 100 users and 25 above 100 users.

plans.name: Duo Essentials
plans.notes: Adds phishing-resistant MFA, passwordless authentication, single sign-on and Trusted Endpoints

plans.name: Duo Advantage
plans.notes: Adds Risk-Based Authentication, session theft protection and Duo Passport

plans.name: Duo Premier
plans.notes: Adds VPN-less remote access and device trust with an endpoint protection check

hiddenCosts: Risk-Based Authentication is listed under Advantage and above, so Essentials buyers pay $3 more per user to get it.
Licenses come in blocks of 10 below 100 users and blocks of 25 above, so seat counts round up.
